topic: normal force (axial) - healthy adults
citation: Schomaker LRB, Plamondon R. The relation between pen force and pen-point kinematics in handwriting. Biological Cybernetics 63:277-289
task_or_setup: Cursive Dutch word 'gestaakt' (10 reps) plus drawing patterns (finger lines, wrist lines, CW/CCW circles 5-6 mm, scribbles), 12 s trials at normal pace; lab stylus with strain-gauge axial force transducer (0-10 N) holding a normal ballpoint refill, writing on A4 paper placed on a Calcomp 9000 tablet (105.2 Hz); forearm fixed in a cuff
participants_or_bench: 16 right-handed students (5 M, 11 F), mean age 23.3 y
comparator: Between patterns (cursive vs simple drawing) and between subjects
key_quantitative_findings: Axial pen force (APF) while writing the cursive word: per-subject means 57-212 g (0.56-2.08 N); mean of the 16 subject means 103 g = 1.01 N, between-subject SD 44 g = 0.43 N, median 96 g = 0.94 N (computed by CON from Table 4a); within-word SD 11-25 g (0.11-0.25 N), mean 18 g. Condition means (Table 2): scribbles 83.6 g, wrist lines 87.5 g, CW circles 108.9 g, cursive 109.7 g (variance 806 g^2, highest), finger lines 113.5 g, CCW circles 115.3 g. Within a trial (maximum 12 s; mean word duration 4.9 s) APF drifted +8 g/s in cursive (linear-fit start 91.6 g, end 127.7 g) and -1 to -2 g/s in drawing patterns. APF only weakly coupled to kinematics (coherence <0.5; mean r(APF, finger displacement) = -0.23).
units_and_conditions: grams-force along the pen axis (APF), not normal to the page (1 g = 9.81 mN); transducer low-pass 2nd-order Butterworth -3 dB at 17.5 Hz, 10-bit; paper on digitiser (hard underlay); forearm immobilised
locator: Methods 2.1-2.2; Results; Table 2 (preprint p.30) and Table 4a (p.31)
limitations: Forearm fixed in cuff (restricts natural writing); 16 young students; single word; hard underlay; axial rather than normal force; 1990 transducer; ballpoint type/ink not specified
relevance_to_design: Direct measure of the axial contact load the moving nib must carry during natural cursive writing with a ballpoint on paper
transferability_reason: Ballpoint refill on paper, adult writers, force measured at the refill exactly where our actuator sits; only posture restriction and underlay differ
design_implication: Use ~1.0 N nominal axial load, between-writer 0.5-2.1 N, within-word SD ~0.2 N and slow upward drift within words when sizing the nib support, actuator holding force and any force sensing
search_query: WebSearch: Schomaker Plamondon 1990 "relation between pen force and pen-point kinematics in handwriting"; curl https://www.ai.rug.nl/~lambert/papers/pen-pressure.pdf

topic: pen tilt angle; friction; force/kinematic spectra
citation: Schomaker LRB, Plamondon R. The relation between pen force and pen-point kinematics in handwriting. Biological Cybernetics 63:277-289 (angle, friction and spectral results)
task_or_setup: As CON-01; additional control recordings with a modified tablet controller giving pen angle (accuracy 3 deg), T = 9 s
participants_or_bench: 16 students (spectra); 4 subjects (pen-angle control test)
comparator: Axial vs normal pen force; kinematic vs force spectra
key_quantitative_findings: Pen angle to the writing plane averaged about 50 deg with variation amplitude about 2.5 deg; correlation between axial and normal pen force never below 0.96; authors state orientation variations seldom exceed 10 deg in normal-size cursive (~2.5 mm high 'a'). Friction: cites Dooijes (1984) estimate that ballpoint friction is about 4% of normal pen force in the 0-2 N range. Spectra: all kinematic and dAPF power spectra peak at 2-5 Hz; scribbling peak 4.5 Hz, circling 3.5 Hz; dAPF has relatively more power above 8 Hz (attributed to friction hysteresis and paper irregularities). Authors quote 8-12 strokes/s for adult cursive.
units_and_conditions: Angle between pen long axis and writing plane (altitude); F_N = F_A x sin(angle); spectra of differentiated signals, resolution 0.103 Hz (patterns) / 0.411 Hz (words)
locator: Introduction pp.3-4; Results p.16 (pen-angle control); Results pp.14-15 (PSDFs); Discussion pp.21-22 (Dooijes friction estimate; strokes/s)
limitations: Angle result from only 4 subjects with fixed forearm; the 4% friction figure is a secondary citation of Dooijes (1984), not re-measured; strokes/s is a statement, not tabulated
relevance_to_design: Gives pen altitude for converting axial to normal/lateral load, shows tilt is nearly constant within writing, and flags that contact-force signals carry >8 Hz texture/friction content
transferability_reason: Same physical situation (ballpoint on paper, adults); angle sample small
design_implication: Model nib load with a fixed tilt of ~50-60 deg per writer; the lateral (perpendicular-to-axis) component of the contact force is then ~0.5-0.65 x normal force (cosine of tilt) plus or minus friction, and must be reacted by the actuator; contact-force sensing will see >8 Hz friction/texture noise
search_query: curl https://www.ai.rug.nl/~lambert/papers/pen-pressure.pdf

topic: normal force (tip) and digit grip forces - children on paper
citation: Lin YC, Hsu CH, Lin CF, Hsu HY, Liu JW, Yeh CH, Kuo LC. Pen-grip kinetics in children with and without handwriting difficulties. PLoS ONE 17(6):e0270466
task_or_setup: Tracing numbers 0-9 on A4 paper with a force acquisition pen (FAP): 3 thin-beam digit sensors (thumb, index, middle) plus a button load cell at the ballpoint tip (TBS-5/SLB-50, Transducer Techniques); pen 12 cm long, 1.1 cm diameter, ~30 g; 70 Hz, 6 Hz low-pass
participants_or_bench: 36 typically developing children (7.97 +/- 0.57 y) and 28 children with handwriting difficulties (8.67 +/- 1.42 y)
comparator: Controls vs handwriting difficulties; on-paper vs in-air phases
key_quantitative_findings: Pen-tip force on paper: controls 0.95 +/- 0.29 N, HD 0.77 +/- 0.36 N (p = .023). Average digit forces on paper (controls): thumb 3.07 +/- 1.31 N, index 2.11 +/- 0.77 N, middle 1.34 +/- 0.75 N; in air: 1.56, 1.15, 1.05 N. Force ratio (tip force / sum of 3 digit forces, on paper): controls 0.16 +/- 0.05, HD 0.11 +/- 0.06 (i.e. grip ~6x tip force). Digit force CV 0.35-0.42; 1.3-1.6 force fluctuations/s.
units_and_conditions: N; tip force from a button transducer in the pen tip (axial direction implied by design, not explicitly stated); A4 paper; 6 Hz low-pass (attenuates higher-frequency content)
limitations: Children aged 7-9; tracing task; 6 Hz filter; tip-force axis not explicitly stated; underlay not reported
relevance_to_design: Pen-on-paper tip force and full grip-force budget measured simultaneously with an inking pen
transferability_reason: Paper and ink pen as in our use case, but children tracing numbers rather than adults writing
design_implication: Expect grip forces on the housing of several N (sum ~6 N) while tip force is ~1 N: housing must not transmit grip squeeze into nib position error

topic: axial and grip force - children; before vs after 10-min copy task
citation: Schwellnus H, Carnahan H, Kushki A, Polatajko H, Missiuna C, Chau T. Writing forces associated with four pencil grasp patterns in grade 4 children. American Journal of Occupational Therapy 67(2):218-227
task_or_setup: Handwriting assessment (CHES) before and after a 10-min copy task; instrumented stylus with TekScan grip sensors (barrel 11 mm) on an electronically inking Wacom Cintiq 12WX; grip sampled every 4 ms, axial every 7 ms; pen and tablet calibrated to N
participants_or_bench: 74 grade 4 children (mean 9 y 11 mo); grasps: dynamic tripod 22, dynamic quadrupod 12, lateral tripod 19, lateral quadrupod 21
comparator: Grasp pattern; thumb position (lateral/adducted vs dynamic); CHES 1 vs CHES 2
key_quantitative_findings: CHES 1: mean grip force lateral-thumb 5.62 N vs dynamic 4.23 N (p = .011); mean axial force lateral 0.96 N vs dynamic 0.65 N (p = .022). CHES 2 (after 10-min task): axial lateral 1.23 N vs dynamic 0.88 N (p = .014). Authors: grip and axial forces were not significantly different between CHES 1 and CHES 2. Writing speed 54.6 vs 55.4 letters/min.
units_and_conditions: N; 'axial force (point pressure)' = force applied downward from the writing utensil onto the tablet surface; glass tablet, not paper
limitations: Children; tablet surface (lower friction than paper); group means only in text; pre/post difference not significant despite higher CHES 2 means
relevance_to_design: Calibrated axial and grip forces for a large sample; shows grip ~4-6x axial force
transferability_reason: Calibrated forces but children writing on a glass tablet
design_implication: Grip/axial ~5-6; a heavier grasp style raises axial load ~50%; do not assume a large fatigue increase from this study alone

topic: fatigue - force change over a 10-min writing task
citation: Kushki A, Schwellnus H, Ilyas F, Chau T. Changes in kinetics and kinematics of handwriting during a prolonged writing task in children with and without dysgraphia. Research in Developmental Disabilities 32(3):1058-1064
task_or_setup: Continuous 10-min writing task; grip forces on pen barrel and normal forces on the writing surface recorded throughout
participants_or_bench: 'Large cohort' of grade 4 children with and without dysgraphia (number not in abstract)
comparator: Early vs late in the 10-min task; dysgraphia vs typical
key_quantitative_findings: Horizontal stroke speed, grip force and normal force increased over time while vertical stroke speed decreased, in all children; attributed to physical/psychological fatigue and compensation. No magnitudes in abstract.
units_and_conditions: Not stated in abstract (same Bloorview instrumented stylus/tablet system as CON-05 likely, not confirmed)
limitations: Abstract only; no effect sizes; children; conflicts in part with CON-05 (no significant pre/post change)
relevance_to_design: Direction of force drift during sustained writing
transferability_reason: Children, likely tablet surface, no magnitudes available
design_implication: Include a within-session upward force drift allowance in the load spectrum and in any force-based control; quantify on adults with our pen

topic: pathological force - writer's cramp (dystonia)
citation: Hermsdorfer J, Marquardt C, Schneider AS, Furholzer W, Baur B. Significance of finger forces and kinematics during handwriting in writer's cramp. Human Movement Science 30(4):807-817
task_or_setup: Writing a test sentence with a graphic-tablet pen fitted with a force sensor matrix (grip force against the barrel) plus tablet 'vertical pen pressure'

design_implication: Upper design load must cover high-force writers; do not infer grip or tip force from kinematics alone

topic: Parkinson's disease - force and spectral content of pen motion on paper
citation: Toffoli S, Lunardini F, Parati M, Gallotta M, De Maria B, Longoni L, Dell'Anna ME, Ferrante S. Spiral drawing analysis with a smart ink pen to identify Parkinson's disease fine motor deficits. Frontiers in Neurology 14:1093690
task_or_setup: Spiral tracing on a paper template (max diameter 6 cm, 5 loops, 1.2 cm pitch) with a smart ink pen (147 mm, max diameter 14.65 mm, 48 g; load cell at tip; tri-axial accelerometer and gyroscope; 50 Hz); desk height 72 cm; PD ON medication
participants_or_bench: 29 PD (72.5 +/- 7.4 y, UPDRS III 19.2 +/- 7.7) vs 29 age-matched controls (72.3 +/- 8.3 y)
key_quantitative_findings: PD applied lower but more variable force (arbitrary units): consecutive-peak force difference 8.07 (5.17) vs 11.28 (6.56); force changes 3.74 +/- 0.68 vs 3.09 +/- 0.63 per s. Relative spectral power of pen acceleration, PD vs control: 0-2 Hz 0.52 vs 0.68; 2-4 Hz 0.16 vs 0.13; 4-7 Hz 0.16 vs 0.10; 8-12 Hz 0.15 vs 0.10. Angular velocity: 2-4 Hz 0.18 vs 0.38 (medians); 4-7 Hz 0.51 +/- 0.16 vs 0.36 +/- 0.10; 8-12 Hz 0.21 vs 0.17 (medians). Tremor stability index 4.84 +/- 1.37 vs 6.00 +/- 1.76 Hz.
units_and_conditions: Force in arbitrary (uncalibrated) units; relative band power (dimensionless) from Welch PSD, 0.1 Hz resolution; kinematic signals band-pass 2-12 Hz before some indicators
limitations: Spiral drawing not handwriting; force uncalibrated; 50 Hz sampling; pen-body IMU (includes rotation) rather than tip displacement; filter choices affect band ratios
relevance_to_design: Shows that even healthy elderly controls have a large share of pen angular-velocity power in the 4-7 Hz tremor band during drawing, and that PD shifts power further into 4-12 Hz
transferability_reason: Target population and ink pen on paper, but drawing task and uncalibrated force
design_implication: Frequency separation of tremor from intended motion is weakest in 4-7 Hz; a canceller cannot simply remove 4-7 Hz pen motion without distorting intended strokes of healthy-like writers

citation: Williams BH. Character Trajectories [dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository (donated 2008); spectral/kinematic metrics computed by the CON stream for this ledger
